LESSON: PUNCTUATION MARKS IN GERMAN BRAILLE • HYPHEN • SLASH

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: GRADE
Strand: German Braille Notation
Topic 10.3: Punctuation Marks in German Braille • Hyphen • Slash
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Punctuation Marks in German Braille • Hyphen • Slash, part of German Braille Notation in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 9 GRADE.

Key inquiry question: Why is punctuation marks hyphen and slash important in German braille?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. tactile embossed Braille flashcards with individual punctuation marks (hyphen and slash) and common words to compare with similar Braille punctuation (dash vs. hyphen),

2. take turns in reading aloud simple Braille sentences in German braille book using hyphens and slashes in real-life contexts to construct sentences and share with peers for correction,

3. use refreshable braille displays, Perkins Braille or slate and stylus and write German

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. tactile embossed Braille flashcards with individual punctuation marks (hyphen and slash) and common words to compare with similar Braille punctuation (dash vs. hyphen),
2. take turns in reading aloud simple Braille sentences in German braille book using hyphens and slashes in real-life contexts to construct sentences and share with peers for correction,
3. use refreshable braille displays, Perkins Braille or slate and stylus and write German

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Punctuation Marks in German Braille • Hyphen • Slash together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
Unity: the learner takes turns in reading aloud simple Braille sentences in French braille book identifying hyphens and slashes.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Peer education: the learner guides others to write dictated or self-composed German sentences using hyphens and slashes

appropriately.
